newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli jets strike three times at Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli jets strike three times at Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli aircraft struck at suspected guerrilla targets in southeast Lebanon on Sunday, firing a dozen rockets into hills used as hideouts by Moslem guerrillas, security sources said.
Large columns of smoke rose from the remote, rocky hillsides after the planes struck three times in five minutes, but there were no immediate reports of casualties.

The raids followed a clash between Israeli troops and Moslem guerrillas on Friday in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone in which two guerrillas were killed, according to sources with the pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army militia.

Israel protested on Saturday that Katyusha rockets were fired from Lebanon into northern Israel on Friday. It complained to a five-nation monitoring group that the rockets violated an April ceasefire understanding.

The weekend military activity in south Lebanon -- the last active Arab-Israeli battlefront -- caused concern in Beirut on the eve of U.S.-sponsored donors conference in Washington at which Lebanon will seek up to $5 billion in reconstruction aid.

Lebanese officials argue that their country deserves financial help and investment after making a huge effort to rebuild and to restore economic, political, social and security stability in the country in the past four years.
Beirut newspapers noted gloomily that the weekend fighting in the south did the country's image no good in the eyes of potential donors as the conference approached.

On Sunday morning, the Israeli warplanes twice hit the eastern side of the central Lebanese mountains overlooking the Bekaa valley. They fired eight rockets into remote, rocky hills between the towns of Mashgara and Ain el-Tineh, security sources said.

In a third strike five minutes later they fired four more rockets into the Jabbour hills seven km (four miles) further south, near the edge of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, the sources added.
Two aircraft carried out each strike while four others circled overhead.
The sources said the areas hit were used by pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas to launch attacks on Israeli troops in the occupation zone.
A Hizbollah spokesman in Beirut told Reuters the pro-Iranian movement had no immediate word of any casualties from the strikes.
